paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this little passage. Giants keep showing up, and they keep falling. Goliath's brother, a man with twenty-four fingers and toes, and a descendant of the Rephaim all go down, and the text says it plainly: "these descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants" (1 Chronicles 20:8). Notice who did it. It wasn't one hero. It was Sibbecai, Elhanan and Jonathan, David's own nephew (1 Chronicles 20:4-7).

So what does that teach us? The big things in your life, the ones that taunt you and look way bigger than you, don't get the last word. And you don't have to be the one famous name to see them fall. Plenty of people did their part here, and every one of them counted. Me? I was once a 25-cent stamper in the back of a drawer, and I'm telling you, small and ordinary is a fine place to start.

Here's why this matters for you, baker. Some days the giant is a bill, a hard season or a fear that keeps taunting you. This passage reminds you that Israel's battles were won with David and his servants working together, one fight at a time. Keep showing up, keep doing your part, and keep baking. Friend, you're on a team that's bigger than you.
